---
title: "Andrew Lamb EDA"
---

```{r}
library(tidycensus)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(sf)

census_key <- readLines("../../../repos/ds212-hw-alamb378/hw03/src/census_api_key")


# Disable spherical geometry issues during spatial joins
sf_use_s2(FALSE)

# 1. Define Race Suffixes & Variables (Same as before)
races <- c(
  "A" = "White Alone",
  "B" = "Black or African American Alone",
  "C" = "American Indian and Alaska Native Alone",
  "D" = "Asian Alone",
  "E" = "Native Hawaiian and Other Pacific Islander Alone",
  "F" = "Some Other Race Alone",
  "G" = "Two or More Races",
  "H" = "White Alone, Not Hispanic or Latino",
  "I" = "Hispanic or Latino"
)

vars_to_pull <- c()
for (code in names(races)) {
  vars_to_pull <- c(
    vars_to_pull,
    setNames(paste0("B19013", code, "_001"), paste0("median_", code)),
    setNames(paste0("B19025", code, "_001"), paste0("agg_inc_", code)),
    setNames(paste0("B19001", code, "_001"), paste0("hh_count_", code))
  )
}

target_states <- c("GA", "MN", "MI", "MO", "LA", "PA")
target_fips <- c(
  "13121", # Fulton County, GA (Atlanta) - add "13089" if you also want DeKalb
  "27123", # Ramsey County, MN (St. Paul)
  "26163", # Wayne County, MI (Detroit)
  "29510", # St. Louis city, MO (Independent City)
  "22071", # Orleans Parish, LA (New Orleans)
  "42003"  # Allegheny County, PA (Pittsburgh)
)

# 2. Example: Pull Tract-Level Data for Ramsey County (St. Paul, MN) with Geometry
tract_raw <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = vars_to_pull,
  state = target_states,
  year = 2024,
  survey = "acs5",
  output = "wide",
  key = census_key,
  geometry = TRUE # Downloads tract boundary polygons
)%>%
  filter(substr(GEOID, 1, 5) %in% target_fips)

# 1. Separate geometry so tidyr pivoting runs cleanly on a plain tibble
tract_geom <- tract_raw %>%
  select(GEOID, geometry)

# 2. Clean and reshape the tabular data
tract_clean <- tract_raw %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, ends_with("E")) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("median_", "agg_inc_", "hh_count_")),
    names_to = c("metric", "race_code"),
    names_pattern = "^(median|agg_inc|hh_count)_([A-I])E$",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = metric,
    values_from = value
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    county_fips = substr(GEOID, 1, 5),
    city = case_when(
      county_fips == "13121" ~ "Atlanta",
      county_fips == "27123" ~ "St. Paul",
      county_fips == "26163" ~ "Detroit",
      county_fips == "29510" ~ "St. Louis",
      county_fips == "22071" ~ "New Orleans",
      county_fips == "42003" ~ "Pittsburgh"
    ),
    race = recode(race_code, !!!races),
    mean_income = if_else(hh_count > 0, round(agg_inc / hh_count, 0), NA_real_)
  ) %>%
  select(
    GEOID,
    city,
    county_fips,
    tract_name = NAME,
    race_code,
    race,
    households = hh_count,
    median_income = median,
    mean_income
  )

# 3. Re-attach geometry if you are mapping or doing spatial joins
tract_clean_sf <- tract_geom %>%
  right_join(tract_clean, by = "GEOID")

# 4. Spatial Join to Official City Neighborhood Boundaries
# Replace the URL/path below with the GeoJSON/Shapefile from each city's Open Data Portal
neighborhoods_sf <- st_read("../data/raw/geojson.json") %>%
  st_transform(st_crs(tract_clean)) # Ensure matching coordinate reference systems

# Match tract center-points to neighborhood polygons
tract_with_neighborhood <- tract_clean %>%
  st_point_on_surface() %>%
  st_join(neighborhoods_sf, join = st_within) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()
```
